articles.title: GHSA: Http4s: Ember chunk parser lenience (TE.TE request smuggling)
articles.summary:
## Summary

Ember's chunk decoder parses the size token leniently: it strips leading and trailing whitespace and accepts a leading `+` or `-` sign.  RFC9112 §7.1 defines `chunk-size = 1*HEXDIG`. articles.title: GHSA: Http4s: DigestAuth nonce map grows unbounded
articles.summary:
The `DigestAuth` server middleware's stale-nonce cleanup uses an inverted comparison: it removes *fresh* nonces and stops at the first *stale* one.  Because a new nonce is created for every unauthenticated challenge, an attacker can drive the nonce map to grow without bound until the JVM runs out of heap.

articles.title: GHSA: Http4s Ember HTTP/2 does not enforce SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS
articles.summary:

articles.title: GHSA: Http4s Ember HTTP/2: unbounded inbound body buffering
articles.summary:

received off the wire, not bytes consumed by the application.  Received DATA is buffered in an unbounded per-stream channel.  Flow control therefore
